$comment: THE EDITABLE COPY SOURCE FOR THE WELCOME EMAIL.
This file is the thing to edit. `build.mjs` renders it into `dist/`; nothing else in
this directory contains a sentence a reader will see. Copy and markup drifting apart is
how an email ends up saying one thing in HTML and another in plain text.
After any edit run `node emails/welcome/build.mjs`, which rebuilds everything and
refuses a link with no verified destination, and `node --test emails/`, which refuses
an instruction naming a control the app does not have.
Brand rules the tests hold you to: `bingd.` always lowercase with its full stop; no
exclamation marks; no em dashes; Rank, never rate; movies, not films, as the app says.
$subjectComment: The first is the recommendation. It asks for an answer, and replies are the point of
the email. `Welcome to bingd.` is deliberately absent: it promises a template.

subject.chosen: I built bingd. Tell me what you think.
alternatives: A note from the person who made bingd.

$preheaderComment: The grey line an inbox shows after the subject. 40 to 90 characters. The first of three
places the reply invitation appears: here, the note's last paragraph, and the closer.

preheader.chosen: Hit reply and it comes straight to me. I read every one.
alternatives: A few things worth trying, and an inbox I actually read.

$noteComment: FOUNDER TO EDIT. Rewrite it in your own voice; it is short on purpose (80 to 160 words).
When you are happy with the words, set `status` to "APPROVED". The worker refuses to
mail anybody but a canary while it says anything else, so that one field is the
approval, and it lands in the same commit as the words it approves.
Keep the last paragraph in some form. The reply invitation is why this email exists.
`{{greeting}}` renders as `Hi <first name>,` when the display name starts with
something that looks like a name, and `Hi,` otherwise. Never the handle.

paragraphs: Thanks for giving bingd. a go. I am Suraj, and right now I am the whole team, so this really is me writing.

I built it because I could never say whether a movie was a four or a four and a half. I can always tell you which of two I liked more, though, and answer that enough times and you end up with a list that is actually yours.
It is early, so you will find rough edges. It also gets much better once one friend you talk about movies with is on it.
If something is confusing, if you love something, or if the thing you went looking for is not there, just hit reply. It comes straight to me and I read every one.

$postscriptComment: FOUNDER INPUT. A second, smaller reason to reply. The title is your number one at the
time of writing; swap it for whatever is true when you approve the email (open the title
in bingd., tap Share, and put that id into targets.json founderTitle). Set the whole

postscript.text: P.S. My number one is The Wolf of Wall Street, and people keep telling me that is a red flag. Rank it and tell me I am wrong.

$cardsComment: Three, secondary to the note. A card has EITHER a `target` (a link, which must be a
verified destination in targets.json) OR a `where` (an instruction inside the app with
no link, whose control names email.test.mjs checks against the app's source).
Only one card is a link because only one of these things has a link that lands
somewhere useful. Invite friends lives on the Profile tab and no URL reaches that tab;
Group Picks is a chip on the For you tab with no route at all. A button for either would
open the wrong screen, so both are said plainly instead. See targets.json `rejected`.

items.title: Follow me
items.body: It puts one person in your feed straight away, and I would like to see what you are watching.

items.title: Bring one friend in
items.body: bingd. is better with somebody you already talk about movies with. Tap Profile, then Invite friends, and send them the link. When they join, you follow each other straight away.

items.title: Try Group Picks tonight
items.body: On the For you tab, tap Group Picks and choose who is watching. It finds movies you can all agree on, and it works with anyone you follow, me included.

closer: Whichever of those you try, tell me how it went. Replies come straight to me.
$footerComment: Four short lines, no navigation, no icons, no logo.
The address and the unsubscribe are not padding. This message asks the reader to invite
somebody and to try a feature, which is enough to treat it as commercial email, so it
carries a sender, a physical mailing address and an unsubscribe.
`postalAddress` is a FOUNDER INPUT. The worker refuses to mail the cohort while it is
null, and nothing here will invent one. There is no company, so it is a mailing address
you are willing to publish: a PO box or a virtual mailbox is the usual choice.

footer.signature: bingd. is made by Suraj Kandukuri.
footer.reason: You are getting this one-time note because you made a bingd. account.
